{{Short description|Public research surveys in Venezuela}}
'''Opinion polls in Venezuela''' are of varying quality and have been used to manipulate public opinion.


== The most reliable polling firms in Venezuela ==
The C-INFORMA News Coalition (Medianálisis, Efecto Cocuyo, Cazadores de Fake News and Probox, with the support of the Latin American Center for Investigative Journalism (CLIP)) analyzed 14 polling firms, making it the most serious study in Venezuela for ranking the country's polling firms. [https://orcconsultores.com/ ORC Consultores] -[https://frequency58.com/f/ Frequency58]-, and Consultores 21<ref>{{Cite web |last=Informativa |first=Coalición |date=2024-07-03 |title=Seis encuestadoras sospechosas promocionan coordinadamente a Nicolás Maduro como favorito para el 28-J |url=https://www.medianalisis.org/seis-encuestadoras-sospechosas-promocionan-coordinadamente-a-nicolas-maduro-como-favorito-para-el-28-j/ |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=Medianalisis |language=es}}</ref>.

== Datanalisis ==
According to ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', Datanalisis is "a respected pollster" in [[Venezuela]].<ref name="LosesGrip">{{cite news |url= https://www.wsj.com/articles/maduro-loses-grip-on-venezuelas-poor-a-vital-source-of-his-power-11553014207 |work= Wall Street Journal |title= Maduro loses grip on Venezuela's poor, a vital source of his power |author= Luhnow, David |date= 19 March 2019 |accessdate= 31 July 2024 |archive-date= 24 July 2019 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190724085144/https://www.wsj.com/articles/maduro-loses-grip-on-venezuelas-poor-a-vital-source-of-his-power-11553014207 |url-status= live }}</ref>

== Hinterlaces ==
[[Efecto Cocuyo]] analysed an April 2024 poll by Hinterlaces and concluded that its methodology was inconsistent, citing contradictory dates, a small sample size, high number of undecided voters, and very high margin of error.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Zambrano |first1=Reynaldo Mozo |title=Engañoso: Hinterlaces da 59% de posibilidad de reelección a Maduro |url=https://efectococuyo.com/cocuyo-chequea/enganoso-hinterlaces-encuesta-59-mad/ |website=Efecto Cocuyo |access-date=31 July 2024 |language=es |date=18 April 2024 |archive-date=31 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240731201752/https://efectococuyo.com/cocuyo-chequea/enganoso-hinterlaces-encuesta-59-mad/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=EC12April/> The poll results were published on website Fuser News, alleged by Efecto Cucuyo to be disseminators of Russian, Iranian, Chinese and Venezuelan state propaganda,<ref>{{cite web |title=Investigación sobre oficina de Alex Saab en Moscú generó huracán de desinformación |url=https://www.cazadoresdefakenews.info/investigacion-alex-saab-moscu-huracan-de-desinformacion/ |website=Cazadores de Fake News |access-date=31 July 2024 |language=es |date=26 July 2022}}</ref> and also by [[Telesur]], a state-controlled Venezuelan media company.{{citation needed|date=July 2024}}

== 2024 presidential election ==
{{Further|2024 Venezuelan presidential election#Opinion polls}}

===  Alleged manipulation of polls ===
During the run-up to the [[2024 Venezuelan presidential election]], several news outlets reported on the proliferation of polls favoring incumbent [[Nicolás Maduro]] published since May 2024 by previously unknown polling firms,<ref name= ET28May>{{cite news |url= https://www.eltiempo.com/mundo/venezuela/venezuela-guerra-de-encuestas-por-liderar-voto-para-elecciones-presidenciales-del-28-de-julio-3346982 |language= es |title= ¿Nicolás Maduro o Edmundo González? La 'guerra de encuestas' por quién lidera la intención de voto en elecciones de Venezuela |trans-title= Nicolás Maduro or Edmundo González? The 'poll war' over who leads voting intentions in Venezuelan elections |first= Ana Maria |last= Rodrigues Brazon |date= 28 May 2024 |access-date= 27 June 2024 |work= [[El Tiempo (Colombia)|El Tiempo]] |archive-date= 27 June 2024 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20240627173644/https://www.eltiempo.com/mundo/venezuela/venezuela-guerra-de-encuestas-por-liderar-voto-para-elecciones-presidenciales-del-28-de-julio-3346982 |url-status= live }}</ref><ref name=NTN2Jun/><ref name=Medianli>{{cite web|url=https://www.medianalisis.org/seis-encuestadoras-sospechosas-promocionan-coordinadamente-a-nicolas-maduro-como-favorito-para-el-28-j/|title= Seis encuestadoras sospechosas promocionan coordinadamente a Nicolás Maduro como favorito para el 28-J |date=3 July 2024|website=Medianalisis|access-date=15 July 2024|quote=DataViva, Ideadatos, Insight by Contrapunto, Data Política Consultores, Encuestadora Paramétrica y Mass Behavior Research|archive-date=15 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240715103956/https://www.medianalisis.org/seis-encuestadoras-sospechosas-promocionan-coordinadamente-a-nicolas-maduro-como-favorito-para-el-28-j/|url-status=live |language=es |trans-title= Six suspicious pollsters are promoting Nicolás Maduro as the favorite for 28 July}}</ref> fuelling concerns that some polls were being used as [[Bolivarian propaganda|propaganda tools]] by [[Chavismo]].<ref name="www.lapatilla.com">{{cite web|url=https://www.lapatilla.com/2024/07/15/la-guerra-de-encuestas-se-desata-en-venezuela-en-un-clima-de-propaganda-y-desinformacion/|title=La 'guerra de encuestas' se desata en Venezuela en un clima de propaganda y desinformación|access-date=16 July 2024|website=www.lapatilla.com|archive-date=16 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240716010122/https://www.lapatilla.com/2024/07/15/la-guerra-de-encuestas-se-desata-en-venezuela-en-un-clima-de-propaganda-y-desinformacion/|url-status=live |language=es |trans-title= The 'poll war' breaks out in Venezuela in a climate of propaganda and disinformation}}</ref> These poll results differed significantly from those published by more traditional pollsters, which showed Maduro trailing.<ref name= NTN2Jun/>
	
According to [[Medianálisis]], [[Efecto Cocuyo]], Cazadores de Fake News and Probox, working with the Latin American Center for Investigative Journalism, these polls were being used to discredit opposition candidates<ref name=Medianli/> in what some outlets called a "poll war".<ref name= NTN2Jun/> Polls showing Maduro ahead were predominantly disseminated by media outlets claimed to be pro-Maduro, such as [[Globovisión]], [[El Universal (Venezuela)|El Universal]], [[Venezuela News]], [[Correo del Orinoco (2009)|Correo del Orinoco]] and [[Notitarde|NotiTarde]].<ref name="Gutiérrez-2024a" />
	
Six pollsters consistently placed opposition candidate [[Edmundo González Urrutia|Edmundo González]] in first place, while others placed Maduro in front. Well-known pollsters in the Venezuelan political sphere, such as [https://orcconsultores.com/ ORC Consultores] -[https://frequency58.com/f/ Frequency58]-, Datanalisis, Datincorp, Delphos, and Consultores 21, along with the emerging Poder y Estrategia, indicated that Urrutia had more than 50% of voting intentions.<ref name="www.lapatilla.com" /> Results by lesser-known firms Hinterlaces, ICS Latam, IMC Orientación, and DataViva, among others, showed Maduro with between 54% and 70% of votes.<ref name="www.lapatilla.com" /> Results by CECA Consultores showed a technical tie slightly favoring the opposition.<ref name="www.lapatilla.com" />

===Investigation of pollsters===
On 28 May, [[Colombia]]n newspaper ''[[El Tiempo (Colombia)|El Tiempo]]'' named IdeaDatos and Data Viva as examples of suspicious pollsters.<ref name= ET28May/> [[NTN24]] also singled out Insight in June 2024, writing that "Eight of ten [recent] polls give the winner to the opposition candidate, Edmundo González Urrutia, and the only two that give victory to ...&nbsp;Maduro, are unknown firms and their social media accounts are recent", adding that IdeaDatos and PoliAnalítica "actively campaign for Nicolás Maduro".<ref name= NTN2Jun>{{cite news |url= https://www.ntn24.com/noticias-politica/guerra-de-encuestas-estos-son-los-diez-sondeos-que-perfilan-al-proximo-presidente-de-venezuela-493950 |title= Guerra de encuestas: Estos son los diez sondeos que perfilan al próximo Presidente de Venezuela |language= es   |date= 2 June 2024 |first= Maryorin |last= Méndez |trans-title= Poll war: These are the ten polls that outline the next President of Venezuela |publisher= [[NTN24]] |access-date= 27 June 2024 |archive-date= 27 June 2024 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20240627173647/https://www.ntn24.com/noticias-politica/guerra-de-encuestas-estos-son-los-diez-sondeos-que-perfilan-al-proximo-presidente-de-venezuela-493950 |url-status= live }}</ref><ref name= EN20June>{{cite news |url= https://www.elnacional.com/opinion/se-activa-la-guerra-de-encuestas/ |title= Se activa la guerra de encuestas |language= es |trans-title= The poll war is activated |first= Marcos |last= Hernández López |date= 20 June 2024 |publisher= [[El Nacional (Venezuela)|El Nacional]] |access-date= 27 June 2024 |archive-date= 20 June 2024 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20240620085122/https://www.elnacional.com/opinion/se-activa-la-guerra-de-encuestas/ |url-status= live }}</ref>
	
''[[La Patilla]]'' reported a statement by sociologist Juan Manuel Trak saying that polls in Venezuela are systematically used as propaganda tools to influence public opinion on possible election results, providing examples of manipulated polls for propaganda purposes from both the government and the opposition. Informative Coalition (C-INFORMA<ref>{{Cite web |last=C-INFORMA |first=La Coalición Informativa |date=2024-07-04 |title=Seis encuestadoras sospechosas promocionan coordinadamente a Nicolás Maduro como favorito para el 28-J |url=https://www.elclip.org/encuestadoras-sospechosas-promocionan-coordinadamente-nicolas-maduro/ |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=El Clip |language=es-CO}}</ref>) concluded that six out of fourteen evaluated firms, then-recently created and of dubious credibility, had published 37 public opinion studies used in a strategy to manipulate the electoral climate. They found seven pollsters to be part of a possible information manipulation campaign, six pollsters to be biased in favor of Maduro, and one pollster to be in favor of the opposition.<ref name="www.lapatilla.com" /> 
	
Political scientist Jesús Castellanos, an expert in electoral affairs, recognized the existence of a "poll war" involving pro-Maduro firms showing bias and disseminating [[fake news]].<ref name="www.lapatilla.com" /> Eugenio Martínez, a journalist and director of the monitoring NGO Votoscopio, argued that there was no poll war per se but rather a misinformation strategy facilitated by the absence of independent media.<ref name="www.lapatilla.com" /> Martínez highlighted that the majority of polls favored the opposition, but the size of the gap between the candidates depends on voter turnout. In Venezuela, where voting is not mandatory, higher turnout would increase González Urrutia's advantage, while lower turnout would reduce the difference.<ref name="www.lapatilla.com" /><ref name="Medianli" /> 
	
Venezuelan independent journalism website [[Efecto Cocuyo]] published several detailed exposés of pollsters, alleging faulty methodology, systematic bias in favor of Maduro, and repeated dissemination of their polls by pro-Maduro outlets. Polling firms alleged to be unreliable include IdeaDatos, CMIDE, Parametrica, Hinterlaces, IMC Orientación, and ICS Latam. <ref name= EC12June/><ref name= EC12April/><ref name=EC14May/>
	
====IdeaDatos, CMIDE and Paramétrica====
According to Efecto Cocuyo, election pollster IdeaDatos published its first poll on 6 May 2024 – a 29 April to 3 May 2024 poll – and their data was re-published by multiple news outlets alleged to be "in favor of the [Maduro regime]".<ref name=EC7May>{{cite news |url= https://efectococuyo.com/cocuyo-chequea/ideadatos-encuesta-inconsistente/ |title= Inconsistente: IdeaDatos anuncia primera encuesta en 4 años sin preguntas y ficha incompleta |first= Jeanfreddy |last= Gutiérrez |date= 7 May 2024 |publisher= [[Efecto Cocuyo]] |work= Cocuyo Chequea (Cocuyo Factcheck) |language= es |trans-title= Inconsistent: IdeaDatos announces first survey in 4 years without questions and incomplete file |access-date= 27 June 2024 |archive-date= 27 June 2024 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20240627152425/https://efectococuyo.com/cocuyo-chequea/ideadatos-encuesta-inconsistente/ |url-status= live }}</ref> Efecto Cocuyo stated that IdeaDatos then had no history of publishing its own polls on its Twitter account since its October 2020 creation and until May 2024, and there was "no further evidence of its existence as a company".<ref name= EC7May/>
	
Methodological concerns include erroneous conclusions, statistical and sampling data missing or wrong, and reliability data and margin of error inconsistencies.{{efn|"The technical sheet does not provide details of age groups, geographic or socioeconomic level, which would allow us to know if it is representative of the Venezuelan electoral universe, how the percentage of the sample by cities or states, nor what would be the specific percentage of men and women in each case. Nor does it specify whether the consultations were from one person per household, on public roads, by telephone, internet or mixed."<ref name= EC7May/>}} Efecto Cocuyo found similar problems in the publication of IdeaDatos` second and third polls in May and June, and stated that the firm's website did not list a RIF [tax information], telephone number, email or physical address, the names of directors or employees, or polls from before May 2024.<ref name= EC12June>{{cite news |url= https://efectococuyo-com.translate.goog/cocuyo-chequea/idea-datos-inconsistente-tercera-vez/ |title= Cocuyo Chequea (Cocuyo Factcheck) |language=es|trans-title= IdeaDatos gives 56.1% to Maduro in its third survey, repeating business gaps and statistics |access-date= 27 June 2024}}</ref> Similar ====IMC Orientación====
Efecto Cocuyo reported that on 1 July 2024 IMC Orientación published a poll placing Maduro in the lead, despite the firm's website having been created only days before its first poll and it listing no employees, management, address, phone number, contact email, or social media profiles. Efecto Cucuyo claimed the poll displayed methodological and statistical oddities, such as interviewing 66% women, and 100% of respondents identifying with a political party.<ref name="Gutiérrez-2024b">{{cite web|url=http://efectococuyo.com/cocuyo-chequea/imc-orientacion-reciente-sin-datos/|title= IMC Orientación creó su web dos días antes de su primera encuesta, que le da 45% a Maduro |access-date=16 July 2024|last=Gutiérrez|first=Jeanfreddy|date=3 July 2024|website=Efecto Cocuyo|language=es|trans-title=IMC Orientación created its website two days before its first survey, which gives 45% to Maduro |archive-date=16 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240716013802/https://efectococuyo.com/cocuyo-chequea/imc-orientacion-reciente-sin-datos/|url-status=live}}</ref> The firm uses the same [[web framework]]s as Paramétrica and has a similar web design, in addition to claiming to have numerous studies and publications, without providing evidence. The poll was disseminated by several media outlets considered to be pro-Maduro. These findings led to Efecto Cocuyo classifying the firm as inconsistent.<ref name="Gutiérrez-2024b" /> 
	
====ICS Latam====
According to Efecto Cucuyo, ICS Latam is a polling firm founded in 2012 that had been inactive since November 2023, abruptly returning in July 2024 to publish a survey showing Maduro leading. The lack of updates on their social media, the suspension of their website, and the dissemination of the survey by these media have raised doubts about the accuracy and quality of their data. The survey also presents oddities such as the absence of "None" or "Don't know / Don't respond" categories, and a duration exceeding the recommended period to avoid mixing formed and forming opinions. The poll allegedly lacked a technical sheet, violating Article 82 of the Venezuelan Organic Law of Electoral Processes (LOPE), which mandates its inclusion to ensure transparency, and was disseminated by media outlets such as [[Globovisión]], [[El Universal (Venezuela)|El Universal]], [[Venezuela News]], [[Correo del Orinoco]] and [[Notitarde]], known for being part of a network of proxy media for sociopolitical misinformation in Venezuela.<ref name="Gutiérrez-2024a">{{cite web|url=http://efectococuyo.com/cocuyo-chequea/ics-latam-encuestadora-inconsistette/|title=ICS resucitó para publicar encuesta inconsistente con 56,9% para Maduro|access-date=16 July 2024|last=Gutiérrez|first=Jeanfreddy|date=11 July 2024|website=Efecto Cocuyo|language=es|trans-title= ICS resurrected to publish inconsistent survey with 56.9% for Maduro|archive-date=16 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240716013432/https://efectococuyo.com/cocuyo-chequea/ics-latam-encuestadora-inconsistette/|url-status=live}}</ref>
